title: What Pakistan Will and Won’t Do in Yemen
gist: Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan activated defense commitments under the August 2026 Mecca Defense Alliance on October 5 after weeks of Houthi drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia. The Houthi conflict is the pact's first major test, forcing it to prove military value without becoming an interventionist force stuck in attrition.

insights.claim: On October 5, 2026, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan moved to activate defense commitments and provide military capabilities agreed under the Mecca Defense Alliance, signed on August 7, 2026.
insights.speaker: Qamar Cheema
insights.so_what: A new trilateral Sunni defense bloc is moving from paper to operations, changing Gulf security calculus.
insights.quote: On October 5, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan moved ahead to activate their defense commitments

insights.claim: The activation of the Mecca Defense Alliance was triggered by weeks of Houthi drone and missile strikes against Saudi Arabia.
insights.speaker: Qamar Cheema
insights.so_what: Sustained strikes on Saudi territory raise risk premia on Gulf energy infrastructure.

insights.claim: In autumn 2026 the Houthis were ramping up ground operations along the Red Sea coast while conducting drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia.
insights.speaker: Qamar Cheema
insights.so_what: Red Sea coastal fighting threatens shipping lanes and freight/insurance costs.
insights.quote: even as the Houthis were ramping up their ground operations along the Red Sea coast

insights.claim: The Houthi conflict is the first major test of the Mecca Pact, regardless of how the crisis plays out.
insights.speaker: Qamar Cheema
insights.so_what: Outcome will set the credibility of the pact as a deterrent in future Gulf crises.
insights.quote: the Houthi conflict has turned out to be the first major test of the Mecca Pact

insights.claim: The Mecca alliance must show its commitments carry real military value without becoming an interventionist force or getting bogged down in a prolonged war of attrition, implying Pakistan will calibrate and limit its involvement in Yemen.
insights.speaker: Qamar Cheema
insights.so_what: Expect limited, capability-based rather than large ground commitments, constraining escalation scenarios.
insights.quote: without crossing the line into becoming an interventionist force or getting bogged down in a prolonged war of attrition
